info.bio:
Stryper es una banda de Heavy Metal formada en California en 1983.

Se destacaron del resto por el contenido cristiano en sus letras, subcategoría que se conoce como "Christian Rock" (Rock Cristiano) o "White Metal" (Metal Blanco), y a la que también pertenecían con el tiempo cientos de bandas como Whitecross y Narnia. A pesar de esta postura, Stryper se hizo un lugar más que destacable entre el Hard Rock de la época. Su imagen se caracterizaba por los colores negro y amarillo

scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Respuesta evangélica a la popularidad del heavy que transforma su código en un esfuerzo misionero para salvar almas. El grupo más conocido es Stryper, cuyo nombre viene de Isaías 53:5 («por sus llagas fuimos curados»), que debuta en 1985 con Soldiers Under Command, toca un metal clásico y ligero y arroja biblias en miniatura al público. En el otro extremo musical, Vengeance toca un thrash extremo con voces demoníacas y títulos como «Human Sacrifice», que se refieren a la crucifixión. En 1987 hay más de cien grupos, vendidos en librerías cristianas y tiendas normales: un «movimiento musical-misionero».

podcast.title: Acronym Meaning
podcast.body: The band's name, STRIPER, serves as an acronym for "Salvation Through Redemption, Yielding Peace, Encouragement, and Righteousness." This acronym was humorously described as "about a strain and acronym as you're ever going to find." "By the way, Striper stands for salvation through redemption, yielding peace, encouragement, and righteousness, which is about a strain and acronym as you're ever going to find."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Acronym Meaning
podcast.body: The band's name, Striper, is an acronym for "Salvation Through Redemption, Yielding Peace, Encouragement, and Righteousness," described as a "strain" of an acronym. "By the way, Striper stands for salvation through redemption, yielding peace, encouragement, and righteousness."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Distinctive Stage Show
podcast.body: Stryper was known for their unique stage presence, which included dressing in "bumblebee spandex" outfits and dramatically firing Bibles into the audience using "specially designed cannons." "They all dressed in bumblebee spandex and fired bibles into the crowd using specially designed cannons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Image and Stage Antics
podcast.body: The band was known for their distinctive visual image, dressing in "bumblebee spandex," and for their unusual stage performance of firing Bibles into the crowd using specially designed cannons. "They all dressed in bumblebee spandex and fired bibles into the crowd, using specially designed cannons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mainstream Breakthrough
podcast.body: Stryper, an Orange County band, is credited with successfully breaking Christian rock into mainstream consciousness. "It took an orange county band called Striper to break through into mainstream consciousness."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mainstream Breakthrough in the 1980s
podcast.body: Striper was an Orange County band that successfully broke through into mainstream consciousness, becoming known for their unique blend of wholesome messages and metal sound. "It took an orange county band called Striper to break through into mainstream consciousness."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Musical Style and Audience
podcast.body: Their sound was characterized as a blend of Van Halen and Def Leppard. Despite their explicitly wholesome Christian message, Stryper successfully attracted the attention and following of metalheads. "Striper sounded a lot like a cross between Van Halen and Def Leopard. And despite their wholesome message, they attracted the attention to metalheads."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sound and Appeal
podcast.body: Striper's musical style was compared to a cross between Van Halen and Def Leppard, allowing them to attract metalheads despite their explicitly wholesome message. "Striper sounded a lot like a cross between Van Halen and Def Leopard."
